name: Oil Painting / Gouache
visualIdentity: Choose oil or gouache as the primary medium. Oil can show varied paint thickness and visible brushwork; gouache uses matte, opaque color masses. Keep lighting and palette coherent. These are separate media, not behaviors to combine indiscriminately. This is a supplemental reference, not a directly named source-collection style.
suitableUses: Explicit fits include product or editorial introductions, explanatory and illustrated narratives, landscape stories, painted intros, event promos, and social poster loops. Chaptered transitions suit stories with meaningful scene handoffs; storytelling suits a clear premise, development, and conclusion. These are inferred applications, not source claims.
limitations: Avoid generic material filters, forced mixing of impasto and matte gouache, fake brush jitter, glossy effects on gouache, and excessive parallax or busy loops. Omit chapter transitions when boundaries add nothing, obscure cause and effect, or break a continuous shot or loop. Omit story orchestration without meaningful progression or when effects hide essential copy.
palette: No intrinsic palette is specified. The optional new-artwork example uses background #F1E6CF, foreground #3E4C48, accents #9B604C, #A89656, #63818A; these are suggestions, not canonical colors. Preserve task, brand, reference, semantic, and asset colors and their roles. Use discrete tokens; gradients are disabled. Example text contrast is 7.272 for background/foreground; accent pairings listed fail the normal-text target. Verify actual compositing; do not recolor to fix contrast.
motionAndInteraction: Use local repainting, brush reveals, or layered scenery; prepare medium-specific paint layers and coverage masks. Painted scenery may use restrained plane drift; a gouache poster can hold with one or two looping elements. Optional chapter transitions coordinate outgoing/incoming scenes and copy over bounded progress; story states align copy, imagery, and framing. Video uses seekable composition time and reading holds. Interactive HTML may map finite scroll progress to states and reverse deterministically; provide keyboard, touch, reduced-motion, and static behavior as applicable. Do not force motion references unsupported by the actual scene.
audio: No fixed soundtrack or mandatory audio layer is specified. Suggest music, narration, vocals, effects, ambience, or silence from the topic, audience, storyboard, and explicit audio requirements. State assumptions; do not assume assets exist. Synchronize and mix with picture, preserve speech clarity, avoid clipping, and review together.
assetRequirements: Prepare medium-specific paint layers and coverage masks or numbered frames; preserve transparency, consistent dimensions, clear names, and inspect assets. Layered scenery needs separated paint planes; poster loops need their chosen focal element isolated as appropriate. Python and Pillow can preprocess, crop, resize, composite, and make masks or textures. Specialist artwork and motion remain separate from composition/export.
combinations: Keep painted scenes alone when no renderer references are needed. For landscape stories or painted intros, combine with style-101 for separated paint-layer depth, choosing oil or gouache and using shared lighting. For a poster hero or social promo, combine gouache with style-103 layout/loop structure and one focal loop. These are suggestions; preserve palette and avoid incompatible material behavior. Motion-012 chapter transitions and motion-015 storytelling are optional, only when scene geometry and narrative support them.
productionApproach: Select the style renderer and motion engine by visual fidelity and action; each animated property has one owner. HyperFrames is the primary composition, seekable timing, media/audio sync, validation, and export pipeline. Use Remotion only if unavailable or a verified required capability is blocked, recording why; an existing React project alone is insufficient. Integrate deterministic time-driven layers or baked assets. Inspect representative frames and the decoded output, timing, dimensions, frame rate, audio sync, and loop continuity. For interactive HTML, scroll/pointer behavior is delivery-specific, not a video dependency.
